summary: The root ثجج (thjj) primarily describes the abundant and forceful flowing of water, blood, or other liquids. It implies a gushing or pouring forth in large quantities, often with intensity.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: ثَجَّ ثج, (A, L, Msb, K,) aor. ثَجِجَ, (A, Msb, TA,) inf. n. ثَجٌّ, (L, Msb, TA,) or ثَجِيجٌ, (A, TA,) or ثُجُوجٌ, (TA,) It (water) flowed: (K:) or poured forth vehemently, (A, Msb, TA,) or much: or, as some say, it (much water) poured forth: (L, TA:) and and signify the same. (K.) ثَجٌّ also signifies The flowing of the blood of a victim brought for sacrifice to the sacred territory of Mekkeh. (S, K, TA.) ثَجَّهُ, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. ثَجُجَ, (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n.
حَلَبَ فِيهِ ثَجًّا حلب فيه ثجا He milked into it milk abundantly flowing. (TA from a trad.)
ثَجُوجٌ ثجوج A source yielding abundance of water. (TA.) See also ثَجَّاجٌ.

ثَجِيجٌ ثجيج [originally an inf. n. (see 1)] A torrent, or flow. (S, K.) So in the saying, أَتَانَا الوَادِى بِثَجِيجِهِ [ The valley brought us its torrent, or flow ]. (S.) The sound of the pouring forth of water. (TA.) See also ثَجَّاجٌ.

ثَجَّاجٌ ثجاج Water pouring forth vehemently: (Msb:) or poured forth; as also: (TA:) or flowing: (Har p. 138:) or flowing much: (Id. p. 393:) and rain pouring forth vehemently; (S, TA;) as also and: (TA:) and blood poured forth: (TA:) and a cloud pouring forth. (A.) Applied to water [or rain, and to blood,] it may have the meaning of a pass. part. n., or, which is preferable, that of an act. part. n. (IDrd, M.) [Hence,] فُلَانٌ غَيْثُهُ وَبَحْرُهُ عَجَّاجٌ (tropical:) [lit.
مِثَجٌّ مثج: see ثَجَّاجٌ. Also, (K,) or خَطِيبٌ مِثَجٌّ, (A,) (tropical:) An eloquent, or able, speaker or orator; (K, TA;) who pours forth a copious flow of words. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
